learn: After the Civil War, Lincoln's plan was lenient; Radical Republicans in Congress wanted stronger protections for freedpeople.
President Andrew Johnson clashed with Congress and was impeached in 1868 but not removed.
Military Reconstruction divided the South into districts under federal control.
check: Radical Republicans wanted ___ protections for freedpeople.
Military Reconstruction divided the South into...
lessons.try: Compare the Lincoln, Johnson and Radical Republican plans.

learn: The 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments abolished slavery, guaranteed citizenship and equal protection, and protected Black men's voting rights.
Black Americans were elected to office, including Senator Hiram Revels (1870).
Groups like the Ku Klux Klan used terror to reverse these gains.
check: Hiram Revels was the first Black...
lessons.try: Research a Black officeholder during Reconstruction.

lessons.t: The End of Reconstruction and Jim Crow
learn: The Compromise of 1877 removed federal troops from the South.
Jim Crow laws enforced segregation; poll taxes and literacy tests blocked Black voters.
Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) upheld "separate but equal".
lessons.try: Analyse a primary source about Jim Crow.

learn: Steel, oil, railroads and electricity transformed the economy after 1870.
Industrialists like Andrew Carnegie (steel) and John D. Rockefeller (oil) built huge fortunes and monopolies.
Inventions included the telephone (1876) and the light bulb (1879).
lessons.try: Debate: were industrialists "captains of industry" or "robber barons"?

learn: Millions of immigrants arrived from southern and eastern Europe and Asia, many through Ellis Island (opened 1892).
Cities grew rapidly; tenements were crowded and unsafe.
The Chinese Exclusion Act (1882) banned Chinese immigration, reflecting nativism.
check: The Chinese Exclusion Act was passed in...
lessons.try: Read Jacob Riis's "How the Other Half Lives" (1890) and discuss its impact.

learn: The transcontinental railroad was completed in 1869.
Settlers, miners and ranchers moved west; the Homestead Act (1862) offered land.
Native nations lost land through wars and reservations; the Wounded Knee Massacre (1890) killed hundreds of Lakota.
check: The transcontinental railroad was completed in...
lessons.try: Map the transcontinental railroad and Native lands.

learn: Progressives (about 1890-1920) sought to fix problems of industrialisation and corruption.
Muckrakers exposed problems: Upton Sinclair's "The Jungle" (1906) led to food safety laws.
Reforms included antitrust laws, the direct election of senators (17th Amendment) and women's suffrage (19th Amendment, 1920).
lessons.try: Research a muckraker and the reform they inspired.

learn: Theodore Roosevelt's "Square Deal" regulated business and protected consumers and nature.
He created national parks and forests.
Woodrow Wilson created the Federal Reserve (1913) and lowered tariffs.
check: The Federal Reserve was created in...
lessons.try: Compare Roosevelt's and Wilson's reforms.

learn: The US gained Hawaii (1898) and, after the Spanish-American War (1898), Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.
The Panama Canal opened in 1914.
Debates over imperialism questioned whether expansion fit American ideals.
check: The US gained ___ after the war with Spain.
lessons.try: Debate the annexation of the Philippines.

learn: The US stayed neutral until 1917; German submarine attacks and the Zimmermann Telegram pushed it to war.
American troops helped the Allies win in 1918.
Wilson's Fourteen Points proposed the League of Nations, which the Senate rejected.
lessons.try: Analyse the Zimmermann Telegram.

learn: The 1920s brought cars, radio, jazz and a consumer economy.
The Harlem Renaissance celebrated Black art, music and writing: Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston.
Prohibition (18th Amendment, 1920-1933) banned alcohol and fuelled organised crime.
lessons.try: Read a Langston Hughes poem from the 1920s.

learn: Nativism led to immigration quotas (1924).
The Scopes Trial (1925) debated teaching evolution.
The Great Migration moved millions of Black Americans from the South to Northern cities.
check: The Scopes Trial was about teaching...
The Great Migration moved people to...
lessons.try: Map the Great Migration.

units.t: The Great Depression and New Deal

learn: Causes included overproduction, uneven wealth, buying stocks on margin and bank failures.
The stock market crashed in October 1929.
Unemployment reached about 25% by 1933.
check: Buying stocks with borrowed money is buying on...
lessons.try: Make a cause-and-effect chart of the Depression.

learn: Families lost homes and farms; "Hoovervilles" of shacks grew.
The Dust Bowl drove families from the Great Plains to California.
Many Americans blamed President Hoover.
lessons.try: Analyse a Dust Bowl photograph.

learn: Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal offered relief, recovery and reform.
Programmes included the CCC, WPA, Social Security (1935) and the FDIC.
The New Deal expanded the federal government's role.
check: The New Deal was led by...
The New Deal's three Rs are relief, recovery and...
lessons.try: Evaluate which New Deal programme had the most lasting impact.

learn: The US stayed neutral but aided Britain through Lend-Lease.
Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941; the US declared war.
The US fought in Europe and the Pacific.
check: The US fought in Europe and the...
lessons.try: Read Roosevelt's "Day of Infamy" speech.

learn: Factories converted to war production; women worked in industry ("Rosie the Riveter").
Rationing limited goods like sugar, meat and gasoline.
Japanese Americans were unjustly forced into internment camps; Korematsu v. US (1944) upheld it, a decision later condemned.
lessons.try: Discuss the injustice of Japanese American internment.

learn: D-Day (June 6, 1944) began the liberation of Western Europe.
Germany surrendered in May 1945; the US dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, and Japan surrendered.
About 70-85 million people died in the war, including six million Jews in the Holocaust.
check: The Holocaust murdered about ___ million Jews.
lessons.try: Debate the decision to use atomic bombs.

learn: The Truman Doctrine (1947) pledged to contain communism.
The Marshall Plan rebuilt Western Europe.
The Berlin Airlift (1948-1949) supplied West Berlin during a Soviet blockade.
check: Containment aimed to stop the spread of...
lessons.try: Explain the policy of containment with examples.

learn: The Korean War (1950-1953) ended in stalemate.
McCarthyism led to accusations of communism that ruined many careers.
The Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) brought the world near nuclear war.
check: The Cuban Missile Crisis was in...
lessons.try: Analyse the decision-making during the Cuban Missile Crisis.

lessons.t: Vietnam and the End of the Cold War
learn: US involvement in Vietnam escalated in the 1960s; protests grew at home.
The war ended with the fall of Saigon in 1975.
The Berlin Wall fell in 1989 and the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
lessons.try: Make a timeline of the Cold War from 1945 to 1991.

learn: Brown v. Board of Education (1954) ruled school segregation unconstitutional.
Rosa Parks's arrest sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955-1956), led by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.
The Little Rock Nine integrated Central High School in 1957.
check: Brown v. Board was decided in...
The Montgomery Bus Boycott began after the arrest of...
The Little Rock Nine integrated a...
lessons.try: Read about the Montgomery Bus Boycott and its strategy.

learn: Sit-ins, Freedom Rides and marches used nonviolent direct action.
The March on Washington (1963) featured King's "I Have a Dream" speech.
The Selma marches (1965) highlighted voting rights.
check: The March on Washington was in...
lessons.try: Analyse why nonviolence was effective.

learn: The Civil Rights Act (1964) banned discrimination; the Voting Rights Act (1965) protected voting.
Other movements followed: women's rights, Chicano rights (César Chávez), Native American rights and disability rights.
King was assassinated in 1968; the struggle continued.
check: The Voting Rights Act was passed in...
lessons.try: Research one civil rights leader beyond King.

learn: Watergate led to President Nixon's resignation in 1974.
Oil crises and inflation strained the economy.
The environmental movement led to the EPA (1970) and the first Earth Day.
lessons.try: Analyse the Watergate scandal's impact on trust in government.

learn: Ronald Reagan (1981-1989) cut taxes, reduced regulation and increased defence spending.
He negotiated arms reductions with Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev.
The economy grew, but so did the national debt.
lessons.try: Evaluate Reagan's economic policies.

learn: The Cold War ended; the US became the sole superpower.
The internet and personal computers transformed daily life.
The economy boomed under President Clinton.
check: In the 1990s, the US became the sole...
The 1990s saw the spread of the...
lessons.try: Interview someone who remembers the 1990s.

units.t: The United States in the 21st Century

learn: On September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks killed nearly 3,000 people.
The US launched wars in Afghanistan (2001) and Iraq (2003).
Security measures expanded, raising debates about liberty and safety.
check: The war in Afghanistan began in...
lessons.try: Discuss how 9/11 changed American life.

learn: The Great Recession (2007-2009) caused widespread job losses.
Smartphones and social media transformed communication.
Globalisation reshaped jobs and trade.
lessons.try: Analyse how one technology changed society since 2000.

learn: Americans debate issues such as health care, immigration, climate and civil rights.
Barack Obama became the first Black president in 2009.
Informed citizens vote, volunteer, and engage respectfully across differences.
lessons.try: Research both sides of a current policy debate.
